name: colOrderStats
title: Gets an order statistic for each column in a matrix

origin.description: Gets an order statistic for each column in a matrix.
origin.usage:
colOrderStats(x, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, which, dim. = dim(x), ...,
  useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An NxK matrix or, if dim. is specified, an N * K vector.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: An integer index in [1, N] indicating which order statistic to return.

arguments.name: dim.
arguments.text: An integer vector of length two specifying the dimension of x, also when not a matrix. The argument is named with a period so it does not clash with dim.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: The installed function returns one order statistic per selected column. which is asInteger(which). The selected rows are partially sorted with rPsort or iPsort. Integer x stays integer. A missing value anywhere in x is an error. An NA row or column index is an error when the other margin is non-empty.
origin.value: A vector of length K. K is the number of selected columns. The mode is integer when x is integer, and double otherwise.
origin.example:
x <- matrix(1:12, nrow = 4, ncol = 3)
colOrderStats(x, which = 1)

translation.description: Gets an order statistic for each column in a matrix.
translation.usage: colOrderStats(x, rows=None, cols=None, which, dim=None, use_names=True)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A 2-d array whose axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A 1-d vector is accepted when dim is set; it is filled column-major, as R stores a matrix. Integer values stay on the integer path. Floating values are computed as float64. Logical input is rejected. A missing value anywhere in x is an error.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based row subscripts. None selects every row. which is counted on this selection.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based column subscripts. None selects every column. Zeros are dropped, negatives exclude, and logical values are recycled.

arguments.name: which
arguments.text: The 1-based order statistic, after R's asInteger. TRUE is 1. A non-integer double is truncated toward zero. The value must lie in 1 through the number of selected rows.

arguments.name: dim
arguments.text: Two integers giving the number of rows and columns. This is dim. in R. None uses the shape of a 2-d x. A 1-d x is filled in column-major order.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for the R argument useNames. It must be TRUE or FALSE. The result is a plain array, with no names attached.

translation.details: The partial sort lives in the Rust crate colorderstats, ported from matrixStats src/colOrderStats.c. Each selected column is copied and passed to R's rPsort or iPsort. psortKM is not used. The returned value is the element placed at the requested order. Integer input returns int32. A missing value in x is an error before the sort.
translation.value: A vector of length K, one order statistic per selected column. Integer input returns int32. Floating input returns float64.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.roworderstats import colOrderStats

x = np.arange(1, 13).reshape((4, 3), order="F")
colOrderStats(x, which=1)
